questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Firstly, I wanted to go to a German speaking country. Sencondly, I chose Goethe since it offered good courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Overall, I had a very nice exchange semester at Goethe. It is an amazing campus and the city suprised my very much! I can higly recommend to study at Goethe and live in Frankfurt!

I had chose courses with to heavy workload and the courses I wanted to take were mostly cancelled this semester. So my study plan changed a lot. Also, I lived in private student housing outside of the city which lowered my experience of the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Yes, when following the workflow on the mobility sites of both universities it was easy.

Housing on the other hand was very difficult.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: At Goethe there were an online introduction on how to sign for courses, get help ect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: They were very helpfull with quick answering emails and phone calls.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
No- extremely difficult.

I would recommend to apply for private studenthousing as soon as getting accepted. Ex. The Fizz, Katolish studentheim ect.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The main dorms do not accept many exchange students. Search for private housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were housing on campus, but off course super difficult to get.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The courses I found that I wanted to take when applying were mostly canncelled. 

If one has a great interest in math the possibilites were low. Classic economics courses were many offeres.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Goethe international office announce when course list of the up coming semester is online and the exam dates. Then there is a website for each course to see the material taught.

The first week of lectures is such that one try out wanted courses and then you sign up for the exam.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Teachers and try out week.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all classes that I registered for. The examination office were very helpfull to assist such that you understand the sign up process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the try out week!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I had excellent teachers! The staff at the economical faculty has both academic backgrounds and some many years experience in the financial sector working. 

They were really good at having discussions with the students. My experience is overall very positive!

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was below my level at Mathematical-Economics at KU. On the other hand, at Goethe it is expected to be much more active in classes and learn by heart to the exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at Goethe is a bit more practical and dicussion minded compared to science at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Credit Risk - best course! Highly recommend! Excellent teacher!
Asset and Liability Management in Insurance Companies
Insurance and Finance - good teacher
Data Science and Marketing Analytics - Do NOT recommend unrealistic high workload!! 
International Macroeconomics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Credit Risk is probably on top 3 of my favorit courses ever taken. Amazing teacher! But we had a full pensum test every 3rd week + exam. It is the most demaning course on the economics Faculty when it comes to finance.

I can highly recommend Insurance and Finance. Interesting course and good teacher.

Housing DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay a semester fee of 344 €. But from this pulic transportation is included and books from the library.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Items were less expensive compared to Denmark in general.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I general the offers were many.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not attend the sports offers. But Goethe has an organisation for international students "International Studenten Treffen" (IST) where you could sign up for museums, walks, picnic ect. I used that and it was also great to socialize and get friends.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The beginning of the semester there is "friend speed-dating" where you get to know a lot of interesting people. It really helped me to get a network.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Heidleberg and Rudesheim! 

I did not travel much since I had too many tests and papers.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy to adjust. Goethe is a very international school, but the possibility to get German friends were also good.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Go to Erasmus events and IST!! Many people attended the pre-semester langugage courses and got many friends from that. In hin side I should have attended that to get a better network.

There are at least 1 Erasmus events a week- so plenty to attend.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I have worked in Germany before so there were not that much cultural shock for me. But Goethe is a very international school and the benefit is that students from many different schools attend. I loved that you got friends from so many different cultures through the school and Erasmus.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Germans are friendly and very helpfull!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) The campus at Goethe University Westend is excellent! It has several cafes, restaurants and libraries. It is very impressive! You get a real campus feeling.

2) Start housing search as soon as getting accepted

3) Go to Erasmus and IST events. There are so many great offers.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Perhaps sign up for easier courses. I signed up for courses with too heavy workload.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
The most rewarding experience were my friendsships and getting to know people from other countries! Secondly, I had the most best teacher in Credit Risk- enjoyed this course so much!

Also Frankfurt is a very nice city and has the perfect size for a semester. There are many great places to see around in Hessen as well. The Westend Campus is special! It has so much to offer!!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
That I signed up for a Data Science course and ended up in a group of 4. Only me and another person could program and I ended up making 75% of a group project of 4 persons. 

My computer broke down 1 day before an exam that was really difficult.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Goehte is an amazing school. Frankfurt has a lot to offer!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
